info.title: Northstack Private API
info.description:
A REST API for your own scripts, Zapier, Make, or anything else you want to connect to your Northstack workspace. Manage keys from Settings → Integrations → API Keys.

An API key represents your company's integration, not a person — but it can never do more than the person who created it: you can only grant scopes your own role allows, and every request is re-checked against the creator's **current** role (narrow that role and the key narrows with it; deactivate the creator and the key stops working with `401 key_creator_inactive`). A workspace in view-only mode (suspended subscription) answers writes with `403 tenant_suspended`.

**AI assistant tokens** (`nk_mcp_…`, OAuth 2.1 access tokens an assistant gets when a user connects it — see `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`) use this same API but act **as that user**: what they can do follows the user's role — Employee visibility, hidden fields and own-only Time Off included — instead of key scopes.

List endpoints also accept optional filters (query params, none required — omit them for the full list): `q` (text search) on tasks, notes, companies, contacts, opportunities and employees; tasks: `assigneeId` (`me` = the acting user), `status` (`open`/`completed`/`all`), `entityType`, `entityId`, `dueBefore`; opportunities: `companyId`, `pipelineId`, `stageId`, `ownerId`; time off: `status`, `employeeId`, `from`/`to` (overlap), and `scope=calendar` (the team calendar) or `scope=pending-approval` (waiting for the acting user's decision).

**Shifts & timesheets** (scopes `shifts:read`/`shifts:write`, `timesheets:read`/`timesheets:write`) mirror the app's own routes under `/shifts/...` and `/timesheets/...`, run as the acting user with the same rules as the app (location managers schedule their locations, direct managers approve timesheets, everyone sees their own shifts): `GET /shifts?from&to&locationId`, `GET /shifts/mine`, `GET /shifts/locations`, `GET /shifts/availability`, `GET /shifts/{id}/candidates`, `POST /shifts` (creates a draft), `PATCH`/`DELETE /shifts/{id}`, `POST /shifts/{id}/assignments`, `POST /shifts/assignments/{id}/respond`, `GET /timesheets?weekStart&employeeId`, `GET /timesheets/approvals`, `GET /timesheets/reports?from&to&groupBy`, `POST /timesheets/entries`, `PATCH`/`DELETE /timesheets/entries/{id}`, `POST /timesheets/submit`, `POST /timesheets/{id}/decision`. Publishing a week, cancelling shifts and shift settings stay in the app. AI assistants can only change draft shifts.

Every error response is the same shape: `{ "error": string, "code": string }`. A `400` from bad input additionally includes `details`, an array of `{ path, message }` naming exactly which field(s) failed.

**Endpoints mirroring the app (2026-10-20).** Besides the endpoints above, the API serves an allowlist of the app's own routes under the same path without the `/api` prefix — e.g. `GET /projects`, `POST /time-off-policies`, `GET /hr/employees/{id}/time-off-balance` — for projects, time-off policies and balances, catalogs, custom fields, tags, task comments, shifts, timesheets and clock in/out. They run as the acting user, so the app's permissions, relationship rules and plan limits apply as-is, with the app's own request and response shapes. Settings, payroll writes, terminations, payments and billing are not available.

get.description: No scope required. Returns the credential (API key or AI assistant token), the user it acts as (with user.employeeId, their own employee record, or null), their role, the workspace plan/status, and the effective scopes for this request — after narrowing to the acting user's current role.

200.description: The calling credential and its effective scopes

get.description: Requires scope `tasks:read`.

post.description: Requires scope `tasks:write`. A Task is cross-entity — it hangs off exactly one Employee, Company, Contact, or Opportunity in your workspace.

404.description: entityId doesn't belong to your workspace

get.description: Requires scope `tasks:read`.

patch.description: Requires scope `tasks:write`. Send only the fields that change. `entityType`/`entityId` can't be changed — a Task can't move to a different record. Set `completedAt` to an ISO datetime to mark it done, or `null` to reopen it.

delete.description: Requires scope `tasks:write`. No request body. Hard delete — the row is gone; a GET afterward is a 404.

get.description: Requires scope `notes:read`.

post.description: Requires scope `notes:write`. Same cross-entity shape as Tasks, minus assignee/due date/completion — a Note is a record, not a to-do.

delete.description: Requires scope `crm.companies:write`. Optional JSON body. Without it, deleting a Company that still has Opportunities fails with a 400 instead of silently taking them down too.

patch.description: Requires scope `crm.opportunities:write`. There is no separate stage-change endpoint — send `stageId` here, alone or with other fields. If the target stage's outcome is `won` or `lost`, the matching reason field (`winReasonId`/`lossReasonId`) is required in the same request or you get a 400.

get.description: Requires scope `hr.timeoff:read`. Everyone's requests need the acting user to administer time off (the same permission as the app's all-requests view); otherwise — typically an AI assistant for a regular employee — only that user's own requests are returned.

200.description: A page of Time Off Requests

post.description: Requires scope `hr.timeoff:write`. Creates a request only. A user who doesn't administer time off can only request for themselves (`employeeId` may then be omitted). Deciding is gated by "is this person's assigned manager", so only an AI assistant token (which acts as a person) can approve or reject — see `PATCH /hr/timeoff/{id}`. The Employee must already have `timeOffPolicyId` assigned to them. If that policy doesn't require approval, the request comes back already `approved`.

example.decisionNote: Auto-approved — this policy does not require approval

400.description: Validation error, invalid date range, Employee/policy not found, or the policy isn't assigned to this Employee

patch.summary: Approve or reject a time off request (AI assistant tokens only)
patch.description: Requires scope `hr.timeoff:write` and acting as the request's approver, so it only works with an AI assistant token — an API key gets `403 not_allowed_for_api_key`. Body: `{ "status": "approved" | "rejected", "decisionNote"?: string }`.
